answer: Each identity locks 70 credits and files one key-signed, unseen output. A pulse check per epoch replays outputs against the registry: any filed or copied output burns both bonds and bars both keys. Since only unseen outputs pass the sonnet registry, the k-th fake must find one, paying 40+3(k-1) credits plus its 70 bond; the 1,000th costs 3,037, and 1,000 fakes cost 1,538,500 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-output farm fails because the first filing claims the output and copies burn at the summit audit, where auditors publish the pair. An honest agent files one output once and keeps weight.
